title: Pixel-object manifesto (how do you communicate that you're going through a change? you don't. you just show it.)
arc: Question, answer, then a list of three words said by objects: how do you communicate change -> you don't, you just show it -> a ring of pixel objects (the identity) -> action, intention, curiosity -> through one's own ability to -> LOVE spelled by objects replacing letters, which then scatter and are scribbled out.
world: Light paper ground with soft vignette and ink-brush marks (and black-and-red when a word is spoken), hand-drawn brush strokes, a small clean sans; the objects are a cohesive set of 16-bit pixel icons (heart, coin, cap, cassette-deck, vinyl, camera, clapperboard, plant, banknote, gamepad, skateboard, cat, book).
actor: A ring of pixel objects: the one persistent element; it orbits, is struck by brush strokes and ink, breaks apart, and its members take turns to stand in for words and for letters of LOVE.

lines.show: A yellow card with dashed border holds a big 'how'; a quick black bar wipes across and the card turns to paper, the question then writes itself in small type as ink-on-paper with a handwriting stroke trailing the cursor.
lines.handoff: The ink stroke that writes the words is also the cursor that scatters objects.

lines.line: how do you communicate that you're going through a change?
lines.show: The sentence is handwritten on grey-white paper word by word, a pen scribble tracing ahead of the text (pen as cursor); at the end the line is struck by small pixel objects (clapper, coin, camera) flicking across, and the text stretches/fades like motion blur.
lines.handoff: A cyan then blue flare swells from the left edge and the page darkens to black-red.

lines.show: A cyan flare pulls across the page, the page washes red, then black; the question line shrinks left; a red-orange profile head in heat-map colours slides in from the right.
lines.handoff: The head's silhouette arrives as the next line's speaker.

lines.show: 'you dont.' sits small in white at the left beside an orange gradient head in profile; a white ellipse orbits the head once (the thought) then a small flick.
lines.handoff: The head holds, the words change in place at the left.

lines.show: 'you' stays, 'dont' is replaced in place by 'just show it.' as the head fades out toward a grey wash; the orange head dissolves into a grey blob that clears the stage for the ring.
lines.handoff: The wash goes white, and the pixel-object ring assembles at the centre.

lines.show: A circle of pixel icons (heart, coin, cap, camera, vinyl, gamepad, book, clapper, plant, banknote, skateboard, cat) orbits slowly in the centre like a clock face; a black brush stroke sweeps across the ring, and one object at a time is struck and flashes with an orange burst.
lines.handoff: The ring is pushed aside; a single object (camera) takes the stage for the first word.

lines.show: On black the pixel camera tilts in, a red starburst blooms behind it, and the word 'action.' types at the right with a blinking cursor (the camera is the verb).
lines.handoff: The camera exits and the ring returns light to carry the next object.

lines.show: A pixel book slides in on a red ribbon swoosh across black; 'intention.' types beside it with a cursor.
lines.handoff: The ribbon becomes the transition: the camera moves across the ring to the next objects.

lines.show: A vinyl record spins in pixel form on black with red scribbled lines whipping round it; 'curiosity.' is revealed with a white bar swipe; red music notes drift up from the record.
lines.handoff: The ring rebuilds light, then objects scatter.

lines.show: The ring spins up, each object is knocked off the circle by brush swirls and some become black ink blobs, others fly out, leaving the stage nearly empty.
lines.handoff: Ink swirl becomes a hand reaching up.

lines.show: On black a warm-orange hand rises from the bottom; 'through ones' appears at its left, 'own ability' at its right, 'to' types at the fingertips (the hand holds the sentence between its fingers).
lines.handoff: The hand dissolves and the word LOVE starts forming letter by letter.

lines.show: Letters L, O, V, E are set with gaps; while each gap is empty a pixel object takes the place of a letter in turn (heart as the first letter slot, camera as the O, book as V, vinyl as the final O/V), flipping between white and black and red ground with each object, until the real letter replaces it.
lines.handoff: The objects leave and the letters float apart on a white field.

lines.show: The four letters shrink to tiny black glyphs and drift apart across a white page with small dots, each one slowly tumbling; a red thread outlines them.
lines.handoff: Black brush swirls and red scribbles pull the letters together.

lines.show: A tangle of black brush strokes and red loops swallows the letters into a dense ball; the film ends on the scribble.

techniques: object as verb (camera = action, book = intention, vinyl = curiosity)
objects stand in for letters of a word
persistent ring of icons that is struck, scattered and rebuilt
in-place word swap beside a figure ('dont' -> 'just show it')
lessons: Let objects say the abstract word: pair each noun with a physical object so the word gets a face (camera for action).
Keep one ring of related objects as a persistent identity, then spend it: strike, scatter, rebuild.
Use a drawn pen/brush mark as both the writing cursor and the transition so the tool is the story.
Swap the answer word in place next to a steady figure ('you dont.' to 'you just show it.') so the correction is visible.
Let the last word be built from the objects you introduced (LOVE letters from icons) and then undo it with the same brush.
Switch ground between white and black per beat and keep the type small; the objects are the loud thing.
